local_facts.title: LADWP ties its HVAC program to final permit and matching equipment records
local_facts.claim: LADWP’s Consumer Rebate Program says a residential HVAC applicant must have active LADWP electric service, apply after purchase and installation, and submit a paid itemized invoice, matching AHRI certificate, and final approved Building and Safety permit. LADWP may inspect and verify the installation, and program funding is limited.
local_facts.why_it_matters: A Los Angeles installation quote should identify the exact matched equipment and make clear who supplies the permit closeout and installation records. Those documents are useful whether or not a homeowner ultimately applies for an incentive; they show that the installed components and approval trail match the project that was sold.

local_facts.title: An AC installation is permitted work with California compliance steps
local_facts.claim: Los Angeles Department of Building and Safety states that a mechanical HVAC permit is required for any installation or modification of heating and cooling systems. The California Energy Commission says Energy Code field verification and diagnostic testing apply through the Energy Code compliance program; depending on the work, HERS testing may be mandatory and properly permitted work triggers the required testing.
local_facts.why_it_matters: A permitted changeout is more than a condenser swap. The scope needs room for permit processing, inspection, compliance documents, and the appropriate third-party field verification or diagnostic testing. Leaving those items out can turn a low bid into an unfinished job that is difficult to document at resale.

local_facts.title: The coast and the Valley are not one cooling design climate
local_facts.claim: The California Energy Commission’s climate reference lists Los Angeles Airport as Climate Zone 6 and Burbank as Climate Zone 9, and its compliance material requires energy calculations to use official hourly weather data adapted to local design conditions. Los Angeles-area system sizing therefore should use the property location rather than a single citywide rule of thumb.
local_facts.why_it_matters: A coastal home and a San Fernando Valley home can place very different late-day demand on a system. The load calculation, equipment capacity, solar exposure, duct layout and comfort expectations should be set for the actual address before an installer recommends tonnage.

pricing.table_head: Los Angeles changeout ranges, job by job

anchors.label: Mechanical permit for a residential changeout
anchors.detail: The city prices a condensing unit under 25 horsepower at $24.00 and an air handling unit at $24.00, then applies a $90.00 floor once a permit covers two or more items, plus a 3 percent Development Services surcharge and a 6 percent Systems Development surcharge.
anchors.source_name: LADBS mechanical and HVAC permit fee schedule

anchors.label: Duct leakage limit on an altered system
anchors.detail: State prescriptive rules for an altered space-conditioning system require duct leakage testing when heating or cooling equipment is replaced on a ducted system: total leakage at or below 10 percent, leakage to outside at or below 7 percent, or all accessible leaks sealed. Refrigerant charge verification and 300 CFM per ton apply in Climate Zones 2 and 8 through 15.
anchors.source_name: California Energy Commission prescriptive alterations form CF1R-ALT-02-E

anchors.label: Municipal utility heat pump incentive
anchors.detail: The rebate schedule pays $100 per ton for a straight central or split air conditioner at 15.2 SEER2, while a qualifying heat pump earns $1,000 to $1,250 per ton ducted and $1,500 to $2,500 per ton ductless. A paid itemized invoice, matching equipment certificate and final approved permit are required.

anchors.label: Refrigerant limit on new residential systems
anchors.detail: Residential air conditioners and heat pumps, mini-splits included, are limited to refrigerants below 700 global warming potential, with a January 1, 2025 compliance date for manufacture and installation. Components made earlier may still be installed, and repair parts are not restricted.
anchors.source_name: EPA technology transitions HFC restrictions by sector
